record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of microwave heating
record.context_brief: Uniqueness for the full Maxwell-heat system
record.original_question: For the full nonlinear microwave-heating problem coupling Maxwell's equations with the heat equation, where both the electrical conductivity σ(θ) and the thermal absorptivity q(θ) depend on the temperature, does the existence theory obtained by the Galerkin method together with the Schauder fixed point theorem actually give a unique solution?

evidence.quote: It is comparatively easy to prove that (1)–(9) has a solution using the Galerkin method (see [1]) coupled with the Schauder fixed point theorem. More difficult appears to prove that the solution is unique.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the full nonlinear microwave-heating model in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ³ with smooth boundary, on a time interval (0,T). The unknowns are the electric field E(x,t), the magnetic field H(x,t), and the temperature θ(x,t), satisfying Maxwell's equations coupled with the heat equation:

  ε ∂E/∂t − ∇ × H + σ(θ) E = 0   in Ω × (0,T),
  μ ∂H/∂t + ∇ × E = 0           in Ω × (0,T),
  ρ c ∂θ/∂t − ∇·(k ∇θ) = q(θ) σ(θ) |E|²   in Ω × (0,T),

together with standard initial conditions E(·,0)=E₀, H(·,0)=H₀, θ(·,0)=θ₀, the perfect-conductor boundary condition E × n = 0 on ∂Ω × (0,T), and a boundary condition for θ (e.g. θ = θ_b or k ∂θ/∂n + h(θ−θ_b) = 0) on ∂Ω × (0,T). Here ε, μ, ρ, c, k > 0 are given constants (or smooth positive functions), and the electrical conductivity σ : ℝ → (0,∞) and the thermal absorptivity q : ℝ → (0,∞) are given continuous, bounded, positive functions of the temperature θ.

Existence of a weak solution (E, H, θ) to this coupled system can be obtained via a Galerkin approximation combined with the Schauder fixed point theorem. The question is:

Under these hypotheses on σ(θ) and q(θ) (both genuinely temperature-dependent, with no monotonicity or smallness assumption beyond continuity and positive bounds), is the weak solution (E, H, θ) of the coupled Maxwell–heat system unique?
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of weak/global solutions for Maxwell's equations coupled with the heat equation under temperature-dependent electrical conductivity (and related variants with temperature-dependent permittivity) has been established in several works (e.g., Yin's results on Maxwell's equations in an electromagnetic field with temperature effect, and the coupled heat–Maxwell system with temperature-dependent permittivity). Uniqueness has been proved only under additional structural assumptions, such as suitable decay/regularity of σ(θ) and Hölder continuity of θ; for the full nonlinear system with both σ(θ) and q(θ) depending on θ under only general continuity/boundedness hypotheses, uniqueness does not appear to be established in full generality.

status_evidence.title: On Maxwell's Equations in an Electromagnetic Field with the Temperature Effect
status_evidence.snippet: Global weak solution and Hölder continuous temperature established; uniqueness proved under suitable conditions on the conductivity.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness is known only under additional assumptions on σ(θ).

status_evidence.title: The coupled heat Maxwell equations with temperature-dependent permittivity
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for the coupled system with temperature-dependent coefficients; uniqueness in restricted regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is established; uniqueness for the fully nonlinear system remains delicate.

status_evidence.title: Global solutions of Maxwell's equations in an electromagnetic field with a temperature-dependent electrical conductivity
status_evidence.snippet: Global solutions constructed; uniqueness obtained under structural conditions on σ(θ).
status_evidence.claim: Partial uniqueness results exist, not a fully general theorem.
